page.text:
A rigorous inductive proof demands careful epistemic hygiene: the
*induction hypothesis* $P(n)$ is assumed strictly for a fixed, arbitrary
index $n$, and must be used solely to derive the subsequent assertion
$P(n + 1)$. In strong induction (complete induction), all preceding
instances $P(0), P(1), \dots, P(n-1)$ are available as simultaneous
hypotheses, which is particularly powerful when dealing with recurrences
like the Fibonacci sequence or the prime factorization of integers.
